references.text: Pilate had already declared Jesus innocent (Luke 23:4), and his desire to release Jesus in verse 20 is a continuation of this conviction about Jesus' innocence.
Pilate repeats his assessment that Jesus is innocent and suggests releasing him after having flogged him (Luke 23:14-16). Verse 20 shows that Pilate again tries to carry this out.
Also in Luke 23:22, Pilate declares for the third time that he finds no guilt in Jesus, which underscores his repeated attempts to release him.
Matthew's account of Pilate's desire to release Jesus and his understanding that it was out of envy that Jesus was handed over (Matthew 27:15-18), parallel to Pilate's attempt in Luke 23:20.
Mark describes how Pilate wanted to satisfy the crowd, but also offered to release Jesus (Mark 15:9-11), consistent with Pilate's desire in Luke 23:20.
John tells that Pilate sought to release Jesus (John 19:12), which corresponds with Pilate's repeated attempts to set Jesus free in Luke 23:20.
In John 18:38-39, Pilate finds no guilt in Jesus and offers to release him according to the Passover custom, parallel to Luke's portrayal of Pilate's desire to free Jesus.
Peter refers to the fact that Pilate had decided to release Jesus, but the people denied him (Acts 3:13). This confirms Pilate's intention to set Jesus free, as described in Luke 23:20.
